incident.title: Degraded Database Latency with Stale Cache and Stalled Invalidation Queue
incident.description: Production alerts report spiking API Gateway p99 response times and severe database connection pool saturation. Primary database telemetry suggests database strain, but synthetic probes report the database engine is completely healthy while the cache invalidation queue is accumulating a large unconsumed backlog.
incident.headline: High API Gateway p99 Latency (2400ms) & DB Connection Pool Saturation (92%)
incident.details: User-facing services report checkout latency spikes. Initial alert indicates database exhaustion.

strategy_ranking.name: Restart Invalidation Consumer & Drain Backlog
strategy_ranking.description: Restart the stalled queue worker consumer pool and accelerate draining of accumulated cache invalidation events.
strategy_ranking.risk_notes: Slight transient message broker load while processing backlogged events; completely safe for persistent storage.
strategy_ranking.reversibility: High — consumer workers can be paused or restarted without data mutation loss.
strategy_ranking.suggested_command: kubectl rollout restart deployment/cache-invalidation-worker -n services && redis-cli info
preconditions: Verify consumer deployment manifest exists in namespace 'services'

strategy_ranking.name: Apply API Gateway Rate Limiting & Load Shedding
strategy_ranking.description: Enable selective ingress throttling and rate-limiting to shed load from degraded backend tiers.
strategy_ranking.risk_notes: Temporarily degrades client experience with HTTP 429 responses, but prevents total service outage.
preconditions: Verify ingress controller supports dynamic rate-limit patching

strategy_ranking.name: Flush & Restart Cache Cluster
strategy_ranking.description: Perform an immediate hard flush and restart of the cache cluster nodes.
strategy_ranking.risk_notes: Causes immediate 100% cache stampede onto the database, risking total database collapse while queue consumer remains broken.
strategy_ranking.reversibility: Irreversible — completely purges warm cache entries in memory.
preconditions: Confirm database can withstand immediate 100% cache miss load

strategy_ranking.name: Rebuild Missing Database Index Concurrently
strategy_ranking.description: Execute asynchronous CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY to restore missing query index without locking database tables.
strategy_ranking.risk_notes: Moderate transient I/O load during index building; completely eliminates table scans upon creation.
strategy_ranking.reversibility: High — index can be dropped without table mutation.
strategy_ranking.suggested_command: psql -c "CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_customer_created ON orders (customer_id, created_at);"
preconditions: Confirm available disk space for index creation

strategy_ranking.name: Trigger Database Replica Failover
strategy_ranking.description: Force promotion of secondary database replica to primary instance.
strategy_ranking.risk_notes: High operational risk, connection drops during DNS switch, potential data loss if replica has lag, and leaves the cache invalidation root cause untouched.
strategy_ranking.reversibility: Low — requires manual database reprovisioning and resynchronization.
preconditions: Verify read replica replication lag is zero
Confirm primary database is truly unrecoverable

recommendation.executive_summary: Recommended Action: 'Restart Invalidation Consumer & Drain Backlog' (Final Score: 70.46/100). Multi-source diagnostic investigation isolated the root cause to 'Cache Invalidation Consumer Stalled', supported by independent diagnostic evidence. The apparent database latency is reconciled by root-cause analysis.

trade_off_comparison.alternative_advantage: Flush & Restart Cache Cluster offers higher execution speed (100.0/100) and lower operational friction (100.0/100).
trade_off_comparison.rejection_rationale: Flush & Restart Cache Cluster is rejected as the primary action because it does not resolve the stalled queue consumer, and flushing the cache would trigger a dangerous 100% cache stampede onto the already strained database. Recovering the consumer safely restores end-to-end cache invalidation without risking database collapse.

recommendation.grounded_contradiction_analysis: Workload telemetry indicated high database latency and connection pool saturation (92%), while direct synthetic probes showed the database responding in 1.8ms with healthy CPU. This scope tension is explained by the 42,000-message invalidation queue backlog: stale cache keys forced high miss rates (65.8% misses) directly to the database. The database is functioning normally but overwhelmed by upstream invalidation failure.
remaining_uncertainties: Exact root cause of the initial consumer worker OOM crash remains uninspected.
Time required to drain the 42,000 message backlog under current traffic.
